newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-GRAF DECLINES COMMENT ON FATHER'S CONVICTION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF DECLINES COMMENT ON FATHER'S CONVICTION.

text.p: Steffi Graf appeared at a news conference before a Tokyo tournament on Monday, but declined to answer reporters' questions about the conviction of her father for tax evasion.

It was the German's first public appearance before the media since her father's conviction last Friday. Investigators in charge of the tax probe in Germany said on Monday they were still investigating the women's world number one.
Speaking before the opening of the Pan Pacific Women's Open in Tokyo on Tuesday, Graf still looked weary from a flight from Australia but insisted she was in good condition for the event.
"My condition is pretty good," she told a news conference. "I'm fit and ready to play."
Graf, who arrived in Tokyo on Saturday from Melbourne where she suffered a surprise fourth-round defeat in the Australian Open, dodged questions about Peter Graf's conviction for evading taxes.
The issue was not raised at the news conference and only came up when television reporters shouted the question about tax evasion to Graf when she was leaving the room where the conference was held.
In Mannheim, Germany last Friday, a court sentenced Peter Graf to three years and nine months in jail for evading tax on his daughter's earnings.

Graf, 58, was convicted on six counts of actual and attempted tax evasion amounting to 12 million marks ($7.4 million) on Steffi's income, while former family tax adviser Joachim Eckardt received two and a half years for complicity.
Tax investigators had also targeted the tennis player herself. But presiding judge Joachim Plass said that investigation should be dropped.

However, Mannheim prosecutor Hubert Jobski, whose office has been in charge of the tax probe, told Reuters on Monday: "The investigations into Steffi Graf are still going on. We are in charge of the case and will conclude it as soon as we can."
